basis: Efavirenz neurotoxicity characteristically causes cerebellar ataxia and encephalopathy; hepatic and skin injury are not consistent defining manifestations.
Chronic granulomatous infection predominantly involving nasal mucosa; ocular and disseminated lesions are minority manifestations.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly are defining features; intellectual disability occurs in 26/33 (~79%). Renal disease is less consistent in BBS1.
Congenital hypoplastic anemia and intellectual disability define the syndrome; unspecified congenital anomalies do not establish additional organ involvement.
Femoral head osteonecrosis causes bone collapse and hip degeneration; local ischemia does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Chondrodysplasia with severe skeletal deformity, kyphoscoliosis and joint contractures.
Hepatic heme-synthesis disorder; damaging photosensitivity exceeds ~30% among clinical cases because cutaneous forms predominate. Neurologic damage is subtype-dependent.
Carboxyhemoglobin impairs blood oxygen transport; the brain is a principal target of toxicity. Cardiac injury is not established in ≥30% across all severities.
Cutaneous melanoma arising within a congenital melanocytic nevus; metastatic sites are not defining organ involvement.
Benign tumor of the mouth floor; oral tissues belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Lens displacement defines disease; supplied HPO reports joint stiffness in 80-99% and cognitive impairment in 30-79%, although these are atypical for isolated ectopia lentis.
Elevated intracranial cerebrospinal fluid pressure defines the condition; this is not systemic vascular hypertension. Permanent visual injury is not universal.
Carcinoma originates in ovarian epithelium, a reproductive tissue outside the axes; urothelial resemblance does not indicate urinary origin or endocrine dysfunction.
Nonmetastasizing neoplasm originating in the duodenal wall.
A purely psychiatric paraphilic disorder without intrinsic damage to any listed organ axis.
Inherited coagulation protein disorder with abnormal bleeding and impaired prothrombin consumption.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome with cortical malformations; strabismus and kyphoscoliosis each occur in 80-99%. Dental crowding alone does not establish digestive dysfunction.
MERS coronavirus infection primarily injures the respiratory tract; renal injury is concentrated in severe cases and is not established as common across all patients.
TERT-related pulmonary fibrosis and bone marrow failure define the disorder. Cirrhosis is 3/134; osteopenia and reflux are each 35/134, below 30%.
Malignant neoplasm located in the main bronchus.
Inherited intestinal B12 malabsorption causes deficiency and megaloblastic anemia; renal tubular protein-reabsorption dysfunction causes proteinuria in 7/8 despite preserved filtration.
Cardiac conduction block originating at the sinoatrial node.
Cancer arises in the male urethra, which belongs to the urinary axis.
Intellectual disability and skeletal anomalies define syndrome; renal dysplasia and cataract each occur in 30-79%. Dental malocclusion omitted under the four-axis cap.
ID defines syndrome; HPO lists renal hypoplasia, aganglionic megacolon and microphthalmia at 80-99%, despite sparse case data. Hypocalcemia and skeletal findings omitted by cap.
